benchmark_input.env_note: RASBERY_IO_WRITER and RASBERY_XE_ANDERSON are DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Both are adopted defaults as of 2026-08-27 and a baseline must exercise the default path; setting either makes the run an experiment, not a baseline. The [RASBERY][PHYSICS_MODE] and [RASBERY][IO_WRITER] receipts prove which path ran (see adopted_defaults below).

adopted_defaults.io_writer: thread (RASBERY_IO_WRITER unset). Adopted 2026-08-27: byte-identical in every validated configuration (single deck 500/500 datasets, M64 45,312/45,312), +0.6 pct M64 throughput. The v1 baseline was written by the inline path; because the writer thread is byte-identical, this does NOT by itself change the golden.
adopted_defaults.xe_anderson_single: ON (RASBERY_XE_ANDERSON unset, non --batch-mode). Adopted 2026-08-27 as a CORRECTNESS improvement: same fixed point, same tolerance, MASTER reactivity 1.970 -> 1.905 pcm and AO 0.022 -> 0.013, at 1.69x. THIS is what moves the golden - the v1 baseline carried a ~2-3 pcm unconverged-Xe artifact and the v2 trajectory does not.
adopted_defaults.xe_anderson_batch: OFF (RASBERY_XE_ANDERSON unset, --batch-mode). Net-negative in batch (202 vs 216 cases/h at M64) from arrival-width starvation; revisit after Phase 5 slot compaction. A batch golden therefore keeps the v1 Xe trajectory.

golden_outputs.determinism: 500/500 datasets bit-exact (h5diff -r) across all 4 repeats: rep1 vs rep2/rep3/rep4 each report 0 differences on all 500 datasets. Container-level sha256 of rep2-4 not compared to rep1 - HDF5 object-header timestamps differ by construction; h5diff -r is the determinism proof, per protocol (never use cmp).
